The story handles the common theme of a family reunion (likely between an estranged mother and son) with great originality and restraint. Instead of relying on melodramatic tropes, tearful embraces, or overused expressions, the author conveys the characters' history and emotional distance through specific, grounded details—such as the small ferry on a river near Lüneburg, a stubborn outboard motor, the silent calculation of when the bed was made, and the final gesture of handing over the mooring line to work the ferry together. The language is fresh, precise, and entirely free of clichés.
